newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Shells from army area likely killed Filipinos-report.
newsitem.headline: Shells from army area likely killed Filipinos-report.

text.p: A special probe panel said on Wednesday the mortar rounds that killed 11 civilians in an Islamic school in the southern Philippines in March were probably fired from an army-controlled area.
The panel, headed by Roman Catholic priest Eliseo Mercado, said the shells could not have come from the direction of Moslem rebels, as claimed by the military.
Ten Moslem students and their teacher died when mortar rounds hit their school on March 16 during fighting between soldiers and guerrillas of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).

Government and MILF panels holding preliminary peace talks in this southern city created the probe body after the military and the guerrillas accused each other of responsibility for the shelling of the school.

In a report released to reporters late on Wednesday, the panel said experts they consulted confirmed the projectiles came from an area northeast of the school that was "within the control of the Armed Forces of the Philippines".
It said the rounds most likely came from an 81mm mortar and panel members who inspected the army area saw an 81mm mortar there.
"The shells...could not have been fired from MILF mortars," the panel said.
No government comment on the report was available.

The MILF is fighting for an Islamic state in the southern islands and was not a party to the peace accord signed by Manila last September with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front ending a 24-year MNLF-led revolt for autonomy.
